Fire is a rapid chemical reaction that releases heat, light and gases. To burn, a fire needs three things: heat or ignition, oxygen and fuel. These three elements are known as the fire triangle.
Removing any one part of the fire triangle can help extinguish a fire. For example, water may remove heat, a fire blanket may remove oxygen, and clearing combustible material removes fuel.
Smoke and toxic fumes
Smoke contains gases, vapour and tiny particles. Toxic fumes can irritate the lungs and may be especially dangerous for people with asthma, bronchitis or other respiratory conditions.
Smoke can spread very quickly and may be more dangerous than flames.
